title: Create charts using Python to better explore the distribution of corals and sponges around Catalina Island
method: Bathymetry (elevation, m; NAD83 / California Albers EPSG:3310, 88.03 m cells). Slope (degrees) and aspect (degrees clockwise from north, downslope, -1 flat) by Horn's 3x3 method with the true cell size on the elevation surface. Project the 7 658 observations to EPSG:3310, add slope/aspect of the underlying cell to the table, then per VernacularNameCategory (13 categories) mean slope and circular-mean aspect (arithmetic mean kept for comparison); horizontal bar charts.
benchmark_defects: The raster's ESRI header is read by rasterio as LOCAL_CS 'NAD83 / California Albers'; the EPSG code must be inferred.
'Each Coral and Sponge species' is ambiguous (VernacularNameCategory, 13 classes incl. 'fish', vs ScientificName, 96 taxa); both groupings are accepted.
A 'mean aspect' is only meaningful as a circular mean; the arithmetic mean differs by up to 170 deg for some categories. Both are accepted, the circular mean is reported.

The published reference script passes the array dimensions as the np.gradient spacing, multiplies the raster by -1 before computing slope and aspect, and samples the points through a transform built from the point bounding box instead of the raster's own transform.
checks: required: a ~7 658-row point table has a slope column (deg or %) with Spearman >= 0.9 vs gold per-point slope and an aspect column within 25 deg of gold for >= 80 % of points

required: per-category (VernacularNameCategory or ScientificName, categories with n >= 20) mean slope within max(0.5 deg, 20 %) and mean aspect within 25 deg of the gold circular or arithmetic mean, each for >= 80 % of categories (may be separate tables/series) (fallback: group means of the verified per-point columns when the code groups by category inline)

required: the figure saved as CoralandSponge.png draws the per-category mean slope and mean aspect (bar lengths, marker/line positions or polar angle; one series each, matched one-to-one to >= 80 % of categories with n >= 20 within the check-3 tolerances; series must have <= 2.5 x n_categories values and not be evenly spaced; a series made mostly of exact per-point values is a raw-point plot and is ignored; when >= 80 % of a series' values equal exactly one of the agent's own per-category numbers, the values are tied to those category labels and compared category by category instead of as a set)
